note: Mont-Saint-Michel: one hero kit, the abbey on the summit (runs/mont-saint-michel/abbey-kit, built in hybrid mode: Opus and Sonnet sessions through the Message Batches API, Haiku live); batched Haiku fill for the village, the towers and the gates; the ramparts, the tidal flats and the passerelle drawn by irl-copy from the data (place.dress.ramparts, place.flats, place.dress.decks).
common: Scale: 1.4 blocks per metre (a storey is about 4 blocks). For a public catalog for a Minecraft 1.21.1 server: only blocks that exist in 1.21.1 (no pale oak, no "iron_chain" (it is "chain" in 1.21.1), nothing 1.21.4+). This is the real abbey of Mont-Saint-Michel for a hero AERIAL render at golden hour: the camera looks from high over the bay's sands from the south-east, along the passerelle footbridge, up at the rock and its abbey against the sky, so the silhouette (spire, choir, the Merveille's sheer north wall), the roofs and the faces toward the south and east matter most. Placement code sets the module exactly where the real abbey stands, on the real rock, so every dimension, the GROUND map and the heights below are exact; keep to them. Exterior only: no interiors beyond what shows through windows and the cloister's arcades. No villagers. Nothing may leave its plot or exceed its stated height. Light it for dusk (warm lanterns on the terraces and stairs, floodlit granite, the gilded archangel catching the light) so no mob spawns on a walkable surface.
closing: Use the photograph only as inspiration for character and colour; the footprint, the ground and the heights above are exact.

kits.intro: The Abbey of Mont-Saint-Michel (Benedictine, founded 966; the church 11th century with a Flamboyant Gothic choir of 1446-1521; the Merveille 1211-1228; the spire 1897 by Victor Petitgrand with Emmanuel Frémiet's gilded Saint Michael): the abbey that crowns the granite rock in its bay, built AROUND the summit, its halls stacked down the rock's flanks on three levels. It must read, at a glance, as THIS abbey: one long grey-granite church along the summit (west to east) with steep dark slate roofs; at the crossing, the square tower and the slender, very tall neo-Gothic spire, dark grey with crockets and pinnacles, topped by the GOLDEN archangel with raised sword; the lacy Flamboyant choir at the east end with flying buttresses and pinnacles; on the NORTH side, the Merveille: a sheer three-storey Gothic wall of granite with tall buttresses rising straight off the rock, the cloister on its top (a square garden ringed by a double row of slender colonnettes under a slate roof); on the SOUTH side, the abbots' lodgings (Logis abbatiaux): tall granite ranges with steep slate roofs and tall chimneys stepping down the rock; and at the east foot the fortified entrance (the Châtelet: two round-fronted turrets either side of a steep stair, Belle Chaise behind it).
kits.frame: THE PLOT'S FRAME: the place's own axes: x east, z south (north is low z). The church's axis runs roughly along x: its west front at low x, the choir at high x. y 0 is the plot's lowest ground (the foot of the lodgings on the rock's south-east flank); the rock rises inside the plot to the summit: follow the GROUND map exactly: build every wall down to the ground under it and never float or bury a floor: where the ground falls away (north and south), the buildings get taller from below (that is the abbey: its lower halls are the crypts and cellars that hold the church up on the summit).

plots.label: THE ABBEY
plots.text: the whole abbey over its footprint, following the ROOF HEIGHT map (from the aerial surface model: it catches the roofs but not the thin spire) for the massing of every range. THE CHURCH along the summit at the footprint's highest ground: the nave (granite walls, round-arched Romanesque windows in two tiers, a steep slate roof), the transepts, the crossing tower; the WEST FRONT a plain classical façade over the west terrace (an open granite platform at the church's floor level, with a parapet, at the footprint's west end); the CHOIR at the east end: Flamboyant Gothic, taller and lighter, a ring of chapels, flying buttresses with crocketed pinnacles, tall pointed windows with tracery (glass panes in dark frames). THE SPIRE: on the crossing tower, a slender octagonal Gothic spire, dark grey (deepslate tiles / polished deepslate / blackstone, with small pinnacles at its base and crockets up its edges), rising to the archangel; THE ARCHANGEL Saint Michael in gold (gold blocks, a little gold-coloured detail) standing on the tip with a raised sword: its top at y SPIRE_TOP (the tallest point of the build: it must be exactly there). THE MERVEILLE along the north edge (the north part of the footprint): a sheer granite wall three storeys high above the falling rock with deep buttresses, narrow pointed windows below and tall ones above; on its roof level the CLOISTER (a square of grass ringed by arcades of slender pale columns (quartz pillars, stone brick walls) under a slate lean-to roof). THE LOGIS ABBATIAUX on the south: tall granite ranges, pointed and square windows, steep slate roofs with dormers and tall stone chimneys, stepping down the south face; the Grand Degré, a steep stair climbing between high walls to the church. THE CHÂTELET and Belle Chaise at the east: the fortified gatehouse: two round-fronted turrets with machicolations and a dark arched entry over a stair, a pointed slate roof behind. Materials: weathered grey granite (stone bricks, cracked and mossy stone bricks low down, andesite / tuff for variation, cobblestone at the rock), dark slate roofs (deepslate tiles and their stairs and slabs), lead-grey spire, a little gold. Where the GROUND map shows bare rock inside the footprint between buildings (courts, terraces), pave it with stone or leave the rock (stone, cobblestone).
